06_runbook_phishing.md:step1.raw: Find every recipient of the message in the email gateway log.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step2.raw: Remove or quarantine the message from all mailboxes.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step3.raw: Block the sender domain and the link domain at the email gateway and the perimeter firewall.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step4.raw: For each recipient, check the firewall logs for a connection to the link address, to find who clicked.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step5.raw: If a click is found, open RB-CRED-02 for that user.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step6.raw: Send a warning notice to all recipients.

06_runbook_phishing.md:step7.raw: Record all findings in the incident ticket.

07_runbook_credential_compromise.md:step.raw: Call the real user on the phone number in the user directory and ask if the login was theirs.
Disable the account in the directory and end all active VPN and remote sessions of that account.
Block the attacker source IP at the perimeter firewall.
Reset the password only after step 2, through the helpdesk with identity checks. Require new MFA enrollment.
Review all logins by the account in the last 24 hours and list every system it reached.
If phishing was the source, disconnect the user's laptop from the network.
For every system reached, check for further activity. If a large data transfer is seen, open RB-EXFIL-04.
Keep all logs unchanged as evidence.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step1.raw: Find the attacker IP and all its requests in the web server log.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step2.raw: Block the attacker IP at the perimeter firewall.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step3.raw: Check response codes and response sizes to see if any request succeeded. A normal error is 4xx or 5xx; a large 200 response to an attack request may mean success.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step4.raw: Ask the web team to review the code of the attacked page.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step5.raw: Check the database server logs for matching queries, if they are available.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step6.raw: Check that the SQL injection rule is active on the web server filter.

08_runbook_web_attack.md:step7.raw: Record all findings in the incident ticket.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step1.raw: Find sessions with an unusually large transfer from the source system in the firewall logs. Note the bytes, the times and the destination.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step2.raw: Block the destination address of the transfer.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step3.raw: Keep the evidence: copy the relevant logs. Do not reboot the source server.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step4.raw: Ask the system owner what data the system holds.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step5.raw: Check if file-level audit logs exist. If they do not, record that it is unknown which files were read.

09_runbook_data_exfiltration.md:step6.raw: Inform Legal and Compliance if the system holds finance, HR or customer data.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step1.raw: Check the change calendar for an approved scan that matches the source, the target and the time window.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step2.raw: If it is approved, close the alert as approved activity. Do not escalate.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step3.raw: If it is not approved and the source is external, block the source IP at the perimeter firewall.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step4.raw: If the source is internal, find the device owner and contact them.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step5.raw: Check which scanned ports answered (allowed) or were refused (denied), and whether any login attempts followed.

10_runbook_scanning_recon.md:step6.raw: Watch the source for the next 24 hours.

03_severity_matrix.md:rule1.raw: A phishing email where a click is seen is handled as credential compromise.

03_severity_matrix.md:rule2.raw: Approved activity from the change calendar is not an incident and gets no severity.

01_company_security_rules.md:1.1.raw: Company local time is PKT (UTC+5, no daylight saving). Incident reports must show times in UTC, and may add PKT in brackets.

01_company_security_rules.md:1.2.raw: Different systems log in different time zones. Check the log source sheet before comparing times.

01_company_security_rules.md:2.1.raw: **Confirmed**: directly shown by a log line or table row. Cite the file and line.

01_company_security_rules.md:2.2.raw: **Suspected**: fits an attack pattern but needs a guess to link two things together. Say what the guess is.

01_company_security_rules.md:2.3.raw: **Not enough evidence in the logs**: the logs are silent or missing. Never fill the gap with a guess.

01_company_security_rules.md:2.4.raw: Never write that data was "stolen" or "leaked" unless a log shows the data moving. A large transfer is evidence of a transfer, not of which files were read.

01_company_security_rules.md:3.1.raw: Activity is "approved" only if the change calendar lists the same system, the same person or tool, and a time window that contains the activity.

01_company_security_rules.md:3.2.raw: Approved activity is not escalated. The report must still say why it was closed and cite the change ID.

01_company_security_rules.md:4.1.raw: Use the severity matrix. Use the most critical asset the attacker actually reached (a confirmed login or session).

01_company_security_rules.md:4.2.raw: If one incident has several parts, report each part. The whole incident gets the highest severity.

01_company_security_rules.md:4.3.raw: Separate incidents with no shared evidence are scored separately.

01_company_security_rules.md:5.1.raw: Recommend only actions found in the runbooks. Cite the runbook ID and step number.

01_company_security_rules.md:5.2.raw: Inform people only as listed in the escalation sheet, with the time limit for that severity.

01_company_security_rules.md:6.1.raw: Several rejected MFA pushes followed by an approved push from a new country is treated as a sign of a stolen password.

01_company_security_rules.md:6.2.raw: Two logins by the same user from different places at the same time is a sign of account misuse.
